So it expects static index.html at repo root (or vite). I'll build a static HTML5 game: "CSGO 1.6" — browser FPS with Three.js? Loading Three.js from CDN may fail in offline capture environment? Probably network available (websearch exists). But safer: pure WebGL/canvas raycaster? Actually a solid approach: build a first-person shooter using Three.js from CDN (unpkg) but capture environment might have internet. Risky. Better self-contained: implement a raycasting engine (Wolfenstein-style) on 2D canvas with sprites, guns, bots. That gives CS 1.6 vibes (de_dust2-inspired map) with zero dependencies, works offline, mobile touch controls.

User asks simply "make csgo 1.6". Ambiguous but a playable browser FPS is the goal. Let's do a high-quality raycast FPS:

Features:
- Menu screen with "CS:GO 1.6" title, Play button, map selection maybe.
- Dust2-inspired map: sand walls, crates, doors.
- Weapon: AK-47 style, pistol, knife. Shoot with raycast, muzzle flash, recoil, reload, ammo HUD.
- Enemies (terrorists) with AI: patrol/chase/shoot, health, death animation.
- Round system: kill all enemies, score, health/armor.
- Minimap.
- Sound via WebAudio synthesized gunshots.
- Mobile touch: dual sticks + fire button.
- Pointer lock mouse look.
- Responsive UI with CS-style HUD (health, armor, ammo, money?, radar).

Should be substantial but within reason. Single index.html plus js modules? Static server supports modules. Use separate files: index.html, styles.css, js/engine.js? Simpler: index.html, style.css, game.js. But game.js will be huge. Split into modules: src/raycaster.js? Let's keep ~2-3 files but well-organized.

Actually, maybe Three.js gives better visual quality, but raycasting canvas can look quite good with textures drawn procedurally, wall shading, floor/ceiling casting. Raycaster is deterministic and no deps — good for capture reliability.

Let's design:

Rendering: 2.5D raycaster at internal resolution scaled to canvas width (e.g. 480x270 upscaled to 1440x900 with pixelated but smooth?). Use canvas draw at e.g. 640 wide for performance, then CSS scale. Add gradient shading, textured walls via procedural texture atlas generated in offscreen canvases (sand bricks, crates, metal). Floor/ceiling: simple gradients + horizontal shadows to save perf. Sprites: enemies drawn on offscreen canvas frames (procedural soldier sprites: standing, walking, shooting, dead) with depth buffer per column. Weapon viewmodel drawn on 2D overlay canvas with procedural AK/pistol/knife shapes, recoil animation.

That's a lot of code but doable. Let's aim for quality but manageable (~1200 lines total).

Game structure:
- Map grid e.g. 32x32 with chars: '#' wall, '.' floor, 'B' brick? Use tile types 1..3 wall textures, 0 empty.
- Dust2-like layout: mid doors, long A, tunnels. Simple symmetric layout with crates as wall tiles.
- Enemies spawn at defined points, pathfind toward player using simple grid BFS with line-of-sight.
- Player movement WASD, sprint shift, crouch ctrl, jump (visual bob only), mouse look.
- Shooting: hitscan with ray casting; enemies have hitboxes approximated by distance perpendicular tolerance. Use ray to enemy center: compute closest approach; if within radius and no wall between, hit. Headshot if aim height near.
- Enemies shoot back with probability based on distance and line of sight, damage player, muzzle flash from sprite.
- Rounds: "Round 1", kill 5 enemies to win round, increasing count. Death screen with restart.
- Weapons: 1 = AK-47 (30 rounds, auto), 2 = pistol (12 rounds), 3 = knife. Switch with 1/2/3 or scroll. Reload R.
- Ammo HUD bottom right, health bottom left, armor, money? Add kill feed and round timer.
- Crosshair dynamic spread.
- Hitmarker, blood particles.
- Audio synth: gunshots (noise burst), reload clicks, footsteps, enemy death, round start beep.
- Mobile: left joystick move, right drag look, fire button, reload button, weapon switch buttons.
- Pause menu with Escape.
- Menu with "ИГРАТЬ" button and instructions, map preview.

Also add a top bar "CS 1.6"? User typed "csgo 1.6" — title "CS:GO 1.6" funny. Use title "COUNTER-STRIKE: GLOBAL OFFENSIVE 1.6" maybe just "CS 1.6" with CS:GO styling. I'll title "CS:GO 1.6" and subtitle "Dust II • Browser Edition".

Language: UI in Russian? User wrote Russian. Make UI Russian with CS flavor. HUD health/armor/ammo universal. Menu Russian: "ИГРАТЬ", "КАК ИГРАТЬ". Could include English too. I'll do Russian primary.

Implementation details for raycasting:

Textures: generate 64x64 texture canvases:
- wall brick: sandstone bricks base #b08a5a with mortar lines, noise.
- crate: wood planks with dark border, "AK" stencil? maybe crate texture with cross braces.
- metal/door.
- concrete.

Store as ImageData arrays for fast sampling. Rendering per column:
for x in 0..W-1: cameraX = 2x/W-1; rayDir; DDA; compute perpWallDist; lineHeight = H/perp; draw column with texture sampling from texture data to an ImageData buffer (floor/ceiling gradient colors computed per row). Writing pixel buffer is fastest. At 480x270 = 129600 px per frame, 60fps ~ 7.8M px writes, fine in JS.

Buffer approach:
- screen ImageData W=480,H=270.
- Precompute floor/ceiling gradient per row: ceiling color darker sand, floor darker. Add subtle gradient + vignette.
- For each column store zBuffer[x].
- Draw walls sampling texture at texX, stepping texY.
- Shading: multiply color by fog/light factor based on distance and side; sand ambient. Add simple "sunlight" factor.
- Sprites (enemies, pickups): billboard rendered after walls using zbuffer. Sprite textures are canvases with transparent bg; sample per pixel, skip alpha<128.
- Then scale buffer to visible canvas via putImageData onto offscreen canvas then drawImage scaled? Use main canvas at low resolution and CSS image-rendering: pixelated with width 100%. But HUD overlays: separate DOM elements for HUD, and weapon canvas overlay drawn at full resolution (or a second canvas on top). Use #game canvas for world (low-res, stretched), #gun canvas full-res for weapon, DOM for HUD/menus.

Weapon viewmodel: draw with canvas paths at bottom right; animate recoil (translate + rotate), muzzle flash polygon, reload dip. Different shapes for AK, pistol, knife (swipe animation on attack).

Enemy sprites: procedural drawing on 48x72 canvas with frames. Could draw stylized terrorist: dark hood, tan vest, gun. Frames: idle, walk1, walk2, shoot, dead. Draw programmatically with simple shapes. Use sprite pool of canvases. Add shadow ellipse on ground? Sprites draw near floor; their vertical position based on distance and sprite scale. We'll place sprite anchored at floor.

Lighting for sprite: tint by distance darkness, and flash white when hit.

Enemy AI:
- state: idle/patrol, alert, attack, dead.
- Each has position, angle, health 100, radius 0.35, speed.
- Line of sight via grid raycast.
- If sees player within range: move toward until distance ~4, strafe, shoot with cooldown 0.9-1.4s, accuracy 0.55 depending distance; damage 8-18.
- If loses sight, move to last known pos.
- Pathfinding: BFS on grid from enemy to player, recompute every 0.5s staggered; move along next cell center. Simple.
- Collision with walls for player/enemies: circle vs grid.

Rounds: spawn N enemies at predefined spawn points far from player. Kill all => round win, +money, round counter, brief banner, next round N+1. Player health resets partially (+25) each round. Death => game over screen with stats (kills, accuracy, rounds). Restart.

Match timer? Round timer 99s; timeout => lose? Add bomb objective? Simpler: deathmatch style "Зачистите карту". Keep rounds.

Map design 32x32 from strings. Need playable layout. Let's author 32 rows of 32 chars. Include open areas, crates, walls, corridors. Tile chars: '#' sandstone wall, 'C' crate, 'D' metal door (wall variant), '.' floor, 'P' player spawn (floor).

Rendering floor/ceiling: Instead of per-pixel floor casting (expensive), gradient rows with slight noise texture? Per-row gradient plus vignette is fine, but flat ground looks bland. Could do actual floor raycasting at half vertical resolution: for each row below horizon, compute rowDistance and texture sample of sand texture with fog. At 480x270, floor rows ~135 * 480 = 65k px extra — okay. Use floor texture (sand with dots) sampled with fog. Ceiling: gradient sky/lamp? Dust2 outdoors — ceiling should be sky! Add distance fog toward sickly tan (dust haze).

Sprite rendering with zbuffer works.

Controls:
- Keyboard: WASD move, Shift walk (or sprint?), Space jump not needed, mouse look with pointer lock, LMB fire, R reload, 1/2/3 weapons, Esc pause.
- Pointer lock on click canvas when playing.
- Mobile: left joystick (move), right half drag to look, buttons: fire, reload, switch weapon. Implement touch joystick via DOM.

UI:
- Menu overlay: dark tactical background, logo, PLAY, controls info, toggle sound? Add "НАЧАТЬ ИГРУ".
- HUD: top center round info / timer, top left radar canvas, top right kill feed? bottom left health/armor with icons, bottom right ammo, center crosshair, hitmarker, damage vignette, kill counter.
- Round banner text center.

- reload: click sequence.

Hit detection hitscan with wall distance:
- ray from player pos direction; step through grid to get wall distance.
- for each alive enemy: vector to enemy; project on ray t = dot; if t>0 and t<wallDist; lateral distance = |cross|; hit if lateral < enemyRadius (~0.32) and height offset check (aim pitch). We have vertical aim (pitch) which in raycaster shifts horizon. Headshot if lateral < 0.12 and maybe pitch within band? Simplify: headshot chance if lateral very small and random? Better: enemy has head at upper part sprite; compute screen-based: since we know distance, enemy body vertical range on screen. Use pitch offset to compute whether aim point at enemy's head zone. Compute aim vertical world height: horizonShift based on pitch. For raycaster, pitching moves horizon; a target at distance d occupies screen. We can convert crosshair's world height at distance d: horizonY = H/2 + pitch; screen center is H/2; relative = H/2 - horizonY... Let me define pitch as pixel offset of horizon (positive = look up? ). Crosshair is at screen center. The world height at distance d corresponding to screen center: h = (H/2 - horizon) * d / (H / ... ) hmm easier: walls are height 1 from floor 0 to 1, projected lineHeight = H/perpDist, wall top at horizon - H/(2*perp), bottom at horizon + H/(2*perp). Wait standard: lineHeight = H/perp; drawStart = -lineHeight/2 + H/2 + pitchOffset. So world y=1 maps to horizon - lineHeight/2 where horizon = H/2 + pitchOffset, world y=0 maps horizon + lineHeight/2. Screen center H/2 corresponds to world y = (horizon + lineHeight/2 - H/2)/lineHeight = 0.5 + (pitchOffset)/lineHeight = 0.5 + pitchOffset*perp/H. So aim height at distance d: yAim = 0.5 + pitchOffset*d/H. Enemy height: feet 0, head 0.85 (scaled maybe 0.9). Head zone y>0.65. So if yAim > 0.62 and lateral<0.16 => headshot. Good.

Enemy sprite should be ~0.9 world height.

Enemy shooting: when LOS and within 12, with cooldown, hit chance decreasing with distance and player movement; damage 7-15, screen flash + directional damage indicator maybe simple red vignette. Enemy muzzle flash sprite frame.

Radar: draw map walls small, player triangle, enemies as red dots only when visible/recent shot? CS radar shows enemies spotted. Show enemies that are alive and in LOS or recently fired, else hidden. Simple: show all when within 10m and LOS, or alerted.

Kill feed: DOM list entries "Вы убили T-01 [AK-47]" fading.

- USP: dmg 24, rpm 400, mag 12, reload 1.8s.

Money? CS has money. Add "$" reward per kill and round; purely cosmetic in HUD. Nice touch: money increases, no shop. Could add buy menu? Overkill. Keep cosmetic maybe skip to reduce clutter. Actually HUD with money adds authenticity. Add `$` counter and kill reward 300. No shop — fine.

- Built a zero-dependency, static canvas raycaster FPS titled “CS:GO 1.6” with a Dust II–inspired map, instead of external Three.js assets, for offline reliability and fast capture.

- Full static game implemented: `index.html`, `style.css`, `js/game.js`, `js/renderer.js`, `js/textures.js`, `js/world.js`, `js/combat.js`, `js/audio.js`.

## 🎮 CS:GO 1.6

A dependency-free, browser-based FPS inspired by Counter-Strike 1.6 and the Dust II map.
Everything is procedural: raycast 3D renderer, textures, sprites, weapon models and WebAudio
sound effects — no external assets or network requests.

### Run

Open `index.html` directly, or serve the folder:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

### Controls

| Action | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` | left joystick |
| Look | mouse (drag if pointer lock is unavailable) | drag on the world |
| Fire | left mouse button | `ОГОНЬ` |
| Reload | `R` | `⟳` |
| Switch weapon | `1` / `2` / `3` or `Q` | `⇄` |
| Pause | `Esc` | `II` |

Clear all terrorists to win the round. Headshots deal bonus damage. Earn cash for kills and
round wins, then survive as long as possible — difficulty rises every round.
